messages:
Nina Park: FYI I'm hitting a pretty annoying UX bug in the Kotlin SDK on Android 14 — calls time out during token refresh and the SDK surface logs "retry suppressed" with no guidance.
Liam O'Connor: can you share logs and which timeout is tripping (call timeout vs socket)?
Nina Park: stack shows okhttp call timeout: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: timeout after ~10s while waiting for write to finish. We then get 401 and the RetryInterceptor tries to retry but okhttp logs: 'retry suppressed: request body not repeatable'.
Priya Nair: sounds like two issues: (1) auth refresh is adding latency that hits the call timeout threshold, (2) body is one-shot so retry can't replay. What's your Call timeout config?
Nina Park: default OkHttp callTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS). We didn't change it in samples. The production apps have higher timeouts but sample quickstart still uses defaults.
Liam O'Connor: default call timeout is pretty low for mobile networks. If auth refresh blocks on network you need to extend call timeout or perform refresh proactively. Also you should surface a clearer error when retry is suppressed.
Nina Park: repro steps: run sample on Pixel 6 emulator, set auth token TTL=2s on mock auth server, stream a ~80KB prompt. Result: write stalls, auth refresh happens, call times out, next retry suppressed.
Priya Nair: short-term fixes: 1) increase callTimeout in quickstart to 1 minute, 2) change sample to use repeatable RequestBody for payloads <= 128KB, 3) log a specific error when suppressed retry occurs with suggested remediation.
Liam O'Connor: agree. Medium-term: SDK should detect when an auth refresh might exceed callTimeout and either extend the deadline during refresh or perform refresh outside the request write path. We can add an option: AuthManager.preemptiveRefreshThresholdMs.
Nina Park: I'm concerned about changing default timeouts broadly. Mobile users expect conservative defaults. Maybe opt for better diagnostics instead: surface telemetry + clear error message and docs pointing to caller-adjustable timeouts.
Priya Nair: makes sense. Also add an example snippet in the Android quickstart:
```
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .callTimeout(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .build()
```
and explain why you might need it when auth refresh could be network-bound.

ci-bot: created issue RD-INF-7896: "android-kotlin: callTimeout too low for auth refresh + non-repeatable body -> suppressed retries; improve diagnostics and sample configs" (labels: devex, sdk, android)

Liam O'Connor: test plan: add MockWebServer scenario that artificially slows auth endpoint so refresh takes >10s and assert that we either succeed with extended timeout or fail with a clear suppressed-retry error. Also add unit test that verifies the diagnostic message appears when a non-repeatable body prevented retry.
Nina Park: I'll patch the sample to use repeatable body for small payloads and add improved logs + quickstart note. PR incoming. :thumbsup:
